concerns.text: Early Trajectory Alignment (cosine similarity between Low-Rank RL and OPD subspace) is tautological. US-2 explicitly requires that 'the update vector lies entirely within the span of the top-k vectors' — this is a hard constraint by construction. Measuring alignment with the subspace that the updates are *projected onto* cannot validate the hypothesis; it only confirms the projection works. This is not an independent test of whether 'foresight' was induced.

The assumption states 'The predictors (OPD subspace vs. RL objective) are not definitionally identical' but then acknowledges 'the projection is an external constraint applied to the RL process.' This is contradictory. If the Low-Rank RL updates are constrained to lie in the OPD subspace, then the OPD subspace IS a deterministic function of the RL updates by construction — they are not independent predictors. The validation cannot use alignment-with-subspace as evidence of causation.

All three primary success criteria (steps-to-80%-accuracy, final subspace alignment, statistical significance) are measured on the same GSM8K subset used for training. Without a held-out test set that is independent of the training data, improvements could reflect overfitting to the specific subset rather than a genuine transfer of 'foresight.' The spec must define a separate validation/test split.

The spec claims the experiment will run in ≤6 hours on CPU with 7GB RAM using a 300M model, but provides no justification or pilot data. A 300M model in FP16 with three independent runs (3 seeds × 3 variants = 9 runs) plus SVD and analysis is a substantial computational load. The assumption about hardware feasibility (stated in Assumptions) is not validated by any preliminary estimate or reference implementation.

FR-005 defines the 'optimal solution' proxy as 'the final accumulated update direction of the standard PPO baseline (unconstrained)' but the Assumptions section acknowledges 'a high-accuracy reference model cannot fit in the defined memory.' This creates a logical inconsistency: if the reference model cannot fit, how is its final update direction computed? The spec must either define a feasible reference or replace this metric with one that does not require an external reference.

The scenario requires computing cosine similarity 'between each variant and the "optimal solution" direction (proxied by the final accumulated update direction of the standard PPO baseline)' but the standard PPO baseline is one of the three variants being compared. Using one variant's trajectory as the reference to evaluate all three variants (including itself) is circular and violates independence of the validation target.

The assumption states the 80% accuracy threshold is 'a community-standard proxy for reasoning competence on GSM8K subsets' but provides no citation or evidence. If this is a standard, cite it; if it is a choice, frame it as such and justify why 80% (not 75%, 85%, or task-specific thresholds) is appropriate for detecting the foresight effect.

The definition states 'A low-dimensional vector space defined by the top-k singular vectors of the aggregated OPD update trajectory' but does not specify how updates are aggregated (concatenation, averaging, weighted sum?) or whether the SVD is computed on the full parameter space or layer-wise (FR-007 mentions 'layer-wise SVD (attention projections only)' but the entity definition does not reflect this constraint).
